violations.issue: Sertraline lacks PBS streamline code and authority requirements notation
violations.suggested_fix: Add PBS streamline code (e.g., 8996K) and note 'PBS authority may be required for doses >100mg or treatment >12 months'

violations.issue: Sertraline starting dose could specify elderly adjustment
violations.suggested_fix: Clarify: 'Start sertraline 50mg daily (25mg daily if elderly or frail, titrate based on response)'

violations.issue: Missing specific monitoring requirements for SSRIs
violations.suggested_fix: Add: 'Monitor for serotonin syndrome, hyponatremia (especially elderly), and bleeding risk if combined with NSAIDs/anticoagulants'

suggestions: Consider adding PBS authority requirements for sertraline (authority required for continued treatment beyond initial trial in some circumstances)
Add note about SSRI withdrawal syndrome if ceasing medication (taper over 2-4 weeks, not abrupt cessation)
Specify baseline investigations before starting SSRI (electrolytes in elderly, bleeding risk assessment if on anticoagulants)
strengths: All drug names use Australian terminology - sertraline, escitalopram (NOT Zoloft, Lexapro brand names)
SSRI selection appropriate for Australian practice (sertraline, escitalopram first-line per eTG Psychiatry)
Correct dosing: sertraline 50mg daily matches Australian therapeutic range (50-200mg/day per AMH)
Appropriate emphasis on combination therapy (SSRI + CBT) aligned with RANZCP guidelines
Safety monitoring mentioned (suicidality in first 2 weeks) - critical for Australian medico-legal practice
No American drug names detected (acetaminophen, epinephrine, etc.)
Medication advice clinically appropriate for major depressive disorder diagnosis

violations.description: Multiple MCQs lack complete SAFE-T framework assessment (particularly access to means, earlier attempts not consistently evaluated)
Depression MCQs deny suicidal ideation but do not provide protective factors or safety planning
Cultural safety elements (Aboriginal/TSI SEWB framework, liaison) not addressed in psychiatric presentations
Low RAG confidence scores (0.0) for newly generated MCQs (ID 2000-2064), indicating potential hallucination risk
Mental State Examination not consistently documented in psychosis/depression scenarios

suggestions: Add complete SAFE-T assessment to all depression/suicidality MCQs (specific plan, access to means, earlier attempts, protective factors)
Include Mental State Examination framework in psychosis/depression scenarios (appearance, behavior, mood, affect, thought form/content, perceptions, cognition, insight)
Add Aboriginal/TSI cultural safety considerations (SEWB framework, Aboriginal liaison offer, trauma-informed approach)
Strengthen RAG citations for newly generated MCQs (ID 2000-2064) - current confidence 0.0 indicates no source verification
Add protective factors assessment to suicide risk MCQs (PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-334, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2004)
Include crisis contacts (Lifeline 13 11 14, Beyond Blue 1300 224 636) in suicide risk scenarios
Specify state jurisdiction for Mental Health Act scenarios (NSW/VIC/QLD differ in criteria and terminology)
strengths: Mental Health Act criteria correctly applied in involuntary admission scenarios (PSY-ANX-BIP-20260125-2002, PSY-SUICIDE-MHA-20260125-2012)
Australian medication names used consistently (olanzapine, quetiapine, sertraline - not brand names)
First-line treatments correctly identified (SSRI + CBT for anxiety/depression, antipsychotics for psychosis)
Acute dystonia management correct (benztropine IM for extrapyramidal side effects - PSY-PSYCHOSIS-20260125-814)
Alcohol withdrawal management appropriate (benzodiazepines + thiamine BEFORE glucose - PSY-FINAL-20260125-610)
Refeeding syndrome correctly identified as critical risk in anorexia nervosa (PSY-FINAL-20260125-2005)
Clozapine monitoring schedule accurate (weekly FBC 18wk → fortnightly to 52wk → monthly - PSY-PSYCHOSIS-20260125-052)
Neuroleptic malignant syndrome correctly diagnosed (rigidity + fever + autonomic instability - PSY-PSYCHOSIS-20260125-144)
